cards.back: Estimates decide the design: 50 writes a second fits one Postgres node, 500,000 does not. You only need to be right to within a factor of ten, and the reasoning matters more than the number.
Memory is about 1,000× faster than an SSD random read; a round trip inside a region is about 10× an SSD read; a trip across a continent is about 100× a round trip inside one region.

cards.front: Round trip inside one data centre
cards.back: About 0.5 ms. Every service hop costs at least this.

cards.front: Round trip across and between continents
cards.back: About 40 to 80 ms across a continent and 100 to 250 ms between continents, which is why CDNs and regional deployments exist.
App server 1k to 10k req/s, Redis about 100k+ ops/s, Postgres a few thousand writes/s comfortably, Kafka 100 MB/s+ per broker, Cassandra 10k to 100k writes/s per node.
86,400, round to 100,000. So 1 million requests a day is about 12 per second, and 1 billion is about 12,000 per second.
99% is about 3.65 days of downtime, 99.9% about 8.8 hours, 99.99% about 53 minutes, and 99.999% about 5.3 minutes.
In series availability multiplies: three services at 99.9% give about 99.7%. Two independent 99% replicas in parallel give 99.99%.
Social feeds 100:1 or more, e-commerce about 10:1, chat about 1:1, logging and metrics mostly writes.
Cold ≈ DNS + 3 round trips (TCP, TLS 1.3, request) + processing + transfer. Warm on a reused connection ≈ 1 round trip + processing + transfer.
Users and actions, requests per second (per day ÷ 100,000 × peak factor), storage with replication, bandwidth, cache memory for the hot 10 to 20%, then turn numbers into decisions.

quiz.q: About how many requests per second is 1 billion requests a day, on average?
quiz.why: 1,000,000,000 ÷ ~100,000 seconds is about 10,000, more precisely about 12,000.

quiz.q: With a 150 ms round trip, roughly what do a cold call's handshakes cost before 50 ms of processing?
quiz.why: DNS aside, TCP, TLS 1.3 and the request are three round trips.

quiz.q: Three services in series each have 99.9% availability. What is the combined availability?
How much downtime per month does 99.99% allow?
quiz.why: 0.01% of a month is about 4.4 minutes.

choices: Random read from a spinning disk
Round trip inside one data centre
quiz.why: An HDD seek is 5 to 10 ms, versus about 0.5 ms for a data-centre round trip.

quiz.q: What peak factor should you plan for over average traffic?
choices: 2 to 3×, more for spiky consumer apps
quiz.why: The page's handy conversions suggest planning for 2 to 3× average.

quiz.q: Roughly how many WebSocket connections can one gateway node hold?
quiz.why: Idle connections are cheap; message rate and memory per connection decide it.
